trials.label: r1c1
trials.name: mask-layout family replica
trials.hypothesis: This copies the only family that scored above 0 elsewhere. The mask goes in under four layouts (as given, y-flipped, x-flipped, transposed) with coordinates, then a 1x1 column stem and a residual 3x3 trunk. Per-type output maps are put back into the four layouts and summed. The net learns which layout matches the world's action indexing, and r<1 keeps the full sample budget. Dev success of 0 on both seeds, with late training success also 0, would mean this world deviates in a way these four layouts do not cover.

trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: full dihedral mask layouts
trials.hypothesis: Same as the replica, with one change: the mask goes in and the outputs come back under all 8 grid symmetries (adding the 180° turn, both 90° turns and the anti-transpose). This covers worlds whose action grid is rotated relative to the observation, which the four-layout family cannot represent. The cost is minimal and r stays below 1. If it scores clearly below the replica, extra layouts dilute learning. If both score 0, rotation is not the deviation.

trials.label: r1c3
trials.name: two action-index orders
trials.hypothesis: New idea: the world might number placement actions cell-first ([Y,X,type]) instead of type-first. Reading the mask as type-first would then scramble it, and every earlier network would fail. This candidate reshapes the mask both ways under the four layouts (8 groups) and sums the outputs written back in both orders. It should succeed where the replica scores 0 if the order deviates. If it scores 0 while the replica succeeds, the extra groups only add noise.

trials.label: r2c1
trials.name: family + global per-action bias
trials.hypothesis: Change: keep the replica network and add a linear layer from the pooled global features to every action logit, starting from small weights. This lets any action index, wherever DONE really sits, learn a stop signal like "nothing is missing". The placement maps stay the same. Refuted if late training success stays at about 0 on both seeds.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
GH = 64
SPATIAL = ["id", "fy", "fx", "tr"]


def fwd_t(t, name):
    if name == "fy":
        return torch.flip(t, [2])
    if name == "fx":
        return torch.flip(t, [3])
    if name == "tr":
        return t.transpose(2, 3)
    return t


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Y = int(spec.Y)
        self.X = int(spec.X)
        self.T = int(spec.n_types)
        self.n_place = int(spec.n_place)
        self.n_actions = int(spec.n_actions)
        sq = self.Y == self.X
        self.spatial = [s for s in SPATIAL if sq or s != "tr"]
        L = len(self.spatial)
        cin = int(spec.in_channels) + L * self.T + 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.out = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, L * self.T, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.out.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.out.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GH, 1)
        self.act_bias = nn.Linear(GH, self.n_actions)
        nn.init.normal_(self.act_bias.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.act_bias.bias)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        m = mask[:, :self.n_place].to(obs.dtype).reshape(B, self.T, self.Y, self.X)
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        ys = ys.view(1, 1, self.Y, 1).expand(B, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        xs = xs.view(1, 1, 1, self.X).expand(B, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        feats = [obs, ys, xs]
        for s in self.spatial:
            feats.append(fwd_t(m, s))
        h = self.stem(torch.cat(feats, dim=1))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(h))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        o = self.out(f)
        place = None
        for k, s in enumerate(self.spatial):
            v = fwd_t(o[:, k * self.T:(k + 1) * self.T], s).reshape(B, -1)
            place = v if place is None else place + v
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1) + self.act_bias(g)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        self.combos = [(o, s) for o in OFFSETS for s in self.spatial]

        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.out = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, L * self.T, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.out.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.out.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_last = nn.Linear(GH, 1)
        self.done_first = nn.Linear(GH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GH, 1)

        B = obs.shape[0]
        P = self.n_place
        mf = mask.to(obs.dtype)
        ms = [mf[:, 0:P].reshape(B, self.T, self.Y, self.X),
              mf[:, 1:P + 1].reshape(B, self.T, self.Y, self.X)]
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)

        x = F.relu(self.c1(h))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        o = self.out(f)
        places = [None, None]
        for k, (off, s) in enumerate(self.combos):
            v = fwd_t(o[:, k * self.T:(k + 1) * self.T], s).reshape(B, -1)
            places[off] = v if places[off] is None else places[off] + v
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        la = torch.cat([places[0], self.done_last(g)], dim=1)
        lb = torch.cat([self.done_first(g), places[1]], dim=1)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
GH = 64
PROJ = 16
HID = 16
SPATIAL = ["id", "fy", "fx", "tr"]


def fwd_t(t, name):
    if name == "fy":
        return torch.flip(t, [2])
    if name == "fx":
        return torch.flip(t, [3])
    if name == "tr":
        return t.transpose(2, 3)
    return t


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Y = int(spec.Y)
        self.X = int(spec.X)
        self.T = int(spec.n_types)
        self.n_place = int(spec.n_place)
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        sq = self.Y == self.X
        self.spatial = [s for s in SPATIAL if sq or s != "tr"]
        L = len(self.spatial)
        G = L * self.T
        cin = int(spec.in_channels) + L * self.T + 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, PROJ, 1)
        self.mixes = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * PROJ, HID, 1) for _ in range(G)])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in range(G)])
        for o in self.outs:
            nn.init.normal_(o.weight, std=0.01)
            nn.init.zeros_(o.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        m = mask[:, :self.n_place].to(obs.dtype).reshape(B, self.T, self.Y, self.X)
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        ys = ys.view(1, 1, self.Y, 1).expand(B, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        xs = xs.view(1, 1, 1, self.X).expand(B, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        feats = [obs, ys, xs]
        for s in self.spatial:
            feats.append(fwd_t(m, s))
        h = self.stem(torch.cat(feats, dim=1))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(h))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        p = self.proj(f)
        place = None
        k = 0
        for s in self.spatial:
            q = fwd_t(p, s)
            outs_s = []
            for (dy, dx) in self.fps:
                if dy * dx == 1:
                    mx, mn, av = q, q, q
                else:
                    qq = F.pad(q, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                    mx = F.max_pool2d(qq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                    mn = -F.max_pool2d(-qq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                    av = F.avg_pool2d(qq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                hh = F.relu(self.mixes[k](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
                outs_s.append(self.outs[k](hh))
                k += 1
            v = torch.cat(outs_s, dim=1).reshape(B, -1)
            place = v if place is None else place + v
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
GH = 64
SPATIAL = ["id", "fy", "fx", "tr"]


def fwd_t(t, name):
    if name == "fy":
        return torch.flip(t, [2])
    if name == "fx":
        return torch.flip(t, [3])
    if name == "tr":
        return t.transpose(2, 3)
    return t


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Y = int(spec.Y)
        self.X = int(spec.X)
        self.T = int(spec.n_types)
        self.n_place = int(spec.n_place)
        sq = self.Y == self.X
        self.spatial = [s for s in SPATIAL if sq or s != "tr"]
        L = len(self.spatial)
        cin = int(spec.in_channels) + L * self.T + 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.bc = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.c3 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.out = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, L * self.T, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.out.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.out.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, GH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(GH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(GH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        m = mask[:, :self.n_place].to(obs.dtype).reshape(B, self.T, self.Y, self.X)
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        ys = ys.view(1, 1, self.Y, 1).expand(B, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        xs = xs.view(1, 1, 1, self.X).expand(B, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        feats = [obs, ys, xs]
        for s in self.spatial:
            feats.append(fwd_t(m, s))
        h = self.stem(torch.cat(feats, dim=1))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(h))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        g0 = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        b = self.bc(g0)[:, :, None, None]
        f = F.relu(f + self.c3(f + b))
        o = self.out(f)
        place = None
        for k, s in enumerate(self.spatial):
            v = fwd_t(o[:, k * self.T:(k + 1) * self.T], s).reshape(B, -1)
            place = v if place is None else place + v
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r4c1
trials.name: obs dihedral stack, identity head
trials.hypothesis: Change: the whole observation goes in under all 8 grid symmetries, together with the mask as given and coordinates. The 1x1 stem can choose a symmetry for each channel, and one per-type map is written straight to the action indices, which always match the mask. This should succeed if the observation, or some of its channel groups, is flipped or rotated relative to the actions. Refuted if late training success stays at about 0 on both seeds.

trials.label: r4c2
trials.name: replica + obs dihedral stack
trials.hypothesis: Change from the replica (r1c1): the observation also goes in under all 8 grid symmetries. The mask still goes in under four layouts, and the outputs are summed back over those layouts. This combines the one family that worked elsewhere with alignment for each observation channel, so it covers deviations inside the observation as well as between observation and actions. Refuted if late training success stays at about 0 on both seeds.

trials.label: r4c3
trials.name: obs dihedral stack, long-horizon recipe
trials.hypothesis: Same network as the first candidate, with a recipe for long-horizon credit: gamma 0.99, gae_lambda 0.95 and 3 PPO epochs, which gives somewhat more samples. Building exactly depends on early placements that leave no extras and a bonus that arrives only at the end of up to 16 steps, so better credit assignment should help once the observation is aligned. Refuted if it scores no better than the first candidate, or about 0 in late training.

analyses.1: There are no trials in this search yet. The starting network scored 0.000 on both seeds. In earlier searches, only one network family scored above 0. It feeds the legal-action mask, reshaped to [type, Y, X], in as input channels under several layouts, adds coordinate channels, and sends that through a 1x1 column stem and a residual 3x3 trunk. Its per-type output maps are put back into the same layouts and summed. That suggests each world differs from its description mainly in how the action indices line up with the observation grid, and that the mask is the only reliable clue to the true layout. Tuning the recipe and choosing heads that assume the stated layout always gave 0. This round I copy the proven family as a baseline at r≈1 with the default recipe, so it trains on the full sample budget. I also try two wider hedges: all 8 grid symmetries, and a second action-index order in which the cell comes before the type. Uniform zeros would mean the deviation lies elsewhere.
analyses.2: Round 1 tried three versions of the mask-layout family: the replica, all 8 grid symmetries and both action-index orders. All six seeds scored 0 on dev, and late training success was at most 0.0005. Even the stochastic training policy almost never finishes an exact build. So the fault in this world is probably not a flip, rotation or type-first versus cell-first numbering of the placement grid. Every plain fill-the-target policy also needs a correct DONE. Placing bricks after the build is complete adds cells outside the target, and 33 placements is far more than the 6 to 16 bricks a target needs. If DONE does not sit at the last index (it might be first, or the action index might be offset), no earlier network could learn to stop. Every trial would then score zero no matter which recipe or trunk it used, which is the pattern seen so far. This round tests that idea directly: a per-action bias that depends on the global state, and a hedge that reads the mask shifted by one index.
analyses.3: Six trials have run in this world, and all six scored 0 on dev. Two of them had a tiny nonzero training success: the plain four-layout replica (0.0005) and the offset hedge plus action bias (0.0003). Neither is a real signal yet. Extra hedges for index order did not help: eight grid symmetries, cell-first ordering, DONE at index 0 and a global per-action bias all gave 0, with exactly 0 training success. So a wrong action index is now an unlikely cause. A more likely cause is that this world is simply harder: an 8x8 base, 6 layers, and designs of up to 16 bricks that must match exactly. If so, the family needs either more samples or a better per-action calculation of where a brick lands and whether that is correct. With 6 trials left, I keep the replica's four layouts and test three single changes: more samples, footprint pooling in action space, and global context fed into the trunk.
analyses.4: All 9 trials scored 0 on dev. The highest late training success was 0.0006, which is noise. Hedges that align the action layout with the observation all failed: 4 and 8 mask layouts, two action-index orders, DONE at either end, and a per-action bias. So did more samples, a footprint pooling head and a global broadcast block. In every trial the mask in its identity layout lines up with the action logits. The mask-layout trick only helps if the mask, under some layout, lines up with the observation. Early in an episode the mask is almost constant, so it gives a weak alignment signal. These trials never tested a deviation inside the observation itself, where each channel group (build, target, missing, extra, heights) may be flipped or rotated relative to the action grid, possibly by different amounts. Untested idea for the last round: feed the observation under all 8 grid symmetries. The 1x1 stem can then pick the right symmetry for each channel and align everything with the action frame.
